pairs.subject: billing-revenue-normalization
pairs.evidence: crates/billing/src/polar.rs:268 Polar's cumulative `order.refunded` total and its per-refund `refund.created` delta are keyed to one shared id, and the store upsert overwrites `amount_minor` with whichever arrives last (it is not monotone), so a second partial refund, or a late delta redelivery, leaves the ledger holding one delta instead of the cumulative refund; the adapters also stamp the FX book version but never the provider's contract version.

techniques.evidence: crates/billing/src/stripe.rs:59 HMAC over raw bytes before JSON parse; constant-time verify_slice; 300s abs tolerance; now passed in; any of several v1 accepted for rotation; missing/malformed header = Signature error. Polar does the same with id.ts.body binding.

crates/billing/src/polar.rs:268 Stripe ids are provider-prefixed and namespaced (stripe:in_x, stripe:refund:ch_x), which is fine. Polar puts a cumulative grain (order.refunded refunded_amount) and a delta grain (refund.created amount) under one key with a last-write-wins upsert, which is the failure the technique names. The collapse test (both_refund_events_for_one_refund_collapse_to_one_id) only uses equal amounts, so it cannot catch this.

crates/billing/src/lib.rs:38 Adapters only return the full record set for one delivery; persistence and acknowledgement live in crates/api/src/billing.rs and the store, judged under cost-and-revenue-governance.

crates/billing/src/fx.rs:241 Per-currency lookup with explicit 0-decimal and 3-decimal lists and a 2-decimal default; codes uppercased; original currency and amount_minor kept on the record; JPY and KWD class tests exist. Small gap: a missing currency field silently defaults to "usd" (stripe.rs:137), and unknown codes are not logged.

crates/billing/src/fx.rs:92 Static JSON book loaded once (shared_fx OnceLock); convention and sources in _meta; base entry and non-positive rates dropped; a missing book falls back to USD-only, loudly; a missing rate is stored 1:1 with converted=false and rate=None; version stamped on each row.

crates/billing/src/stripe.rs:143 Mostly realized: closed 4-kind set, non-negative magnitudes, refunds as separate namespaced records, zero refunds yield no record, kind inferred from the subscription link. But Subscription is assigned even when period_start/period_end resolved to None (Stripe lines[0].period or Polar subscription object absent), which is the recurring-with-nulls case the technique says should be ingested as point-in-time.

crates/billing/src/stripe.rs:168 The rate-book version is stamped but the provider contract version is not: no read of Stripe's envelope api_version or Polar's version, no assertion against an expected version, no version config at registration (BillingRegistry::from_env reads only secrets). A repo-wide grep for api_version/contract_version/Stripe-Version finds only the Anthropic engine client.

pairs.subject: billing-revenue-normalization
pairs.evidence: crates/api/src/billing.rs:119 The webhook handler verifies the signature first, persists the delivery's records in one batch call, and commits the in-flight idempotency claim and returns 200 only after the store returns; a failure drops the claim so the provider's retry is reprocessed, and the margin surface reads caveats and sign from the stored rows.

techniques.evidence: crates/api/src/billing.rs:50 Raw Bytes body and header lookup go to the adapter before anything is parsed; a failure is a 401, logged at warn as a security signal with header values redacted; an authentic untracked event gives an empty vec and is still a 200.

crates/api/src/billing.rs:119 Acknowledged after persist. The delivery-id claim is held in flight, a concurrent repeat gets 409, the claim is marked done only after the store write, and it is released on early exit. Atomicity across records depends on the backend (see notes).
crates/api/src/revenue.rs:48 Manual revenue posts are refused unless amount_usd is a finite, non-negative magnitude ('the sign comes from `kind`'); an inverted period is rejected too.

crates/api/src/revenue.rs:139 The unconverted-currency caveat is read from each row's own converted flag, not from today's book, and is returned in the margin payload as currency_note. revenue_reprice is admin-only, dry-run by default, and stamps a book version, so restatement is a deliberate act.
